title: AttackScenario
description: A white-hat analyst's PREDICTION of how a real attacker could chain two or more of this run's already-gathered findings into a larger compromise. Never a record of anything tested, attempted, or validated -- `status` is locked to the single value "predicted" for exactly that reason: there is no schema-legal way to mark a scenario as confirmed, exploited, or otherwise acted upon. Produced once per run, after every Tier 1 domain's findings are in (engine/attack_scenarios.py), by adapters.mock.attack_scenario (a labeled placeholder) or a live attack-scenario-analyst agent (.claude/agents/attack-scenario-analyst.md).

scenario_id.description: Deterministic fingerprint: sha256 of (run_id, sorted chained_finding_ids, title). Computed by engine/attack_scenarios.py, never by agent judgement.

attacker_goal.description: What a real attacker following this chain would be trying to achieve, e.g. 'exfiltrate customer PII from the analytics data lake'.

narrative.description: Prose walkthrough of the predicted chain, written from the attacker's perspective, in the future/conditional tense (would, could) -- never past/present tense implying it happened.

attack_path.description: Ordered steps of the predicted chain.

based_on_finding_id.description: The finding_id (from this same run) this step is grounded in, or null for a step describing generic attacker tradecraft (e.g. 'pivot using the harvested credential') that isn't itself one of this run's findings.

chained_finding_ids.description: The real finding_ids (from this same run's deduplicated finding set) this scenario chains together. At least two: a single finding is just a finding, not a scenario. engine/attack_scenarios.py verifies every id here actually exists in the run before accepting the scenario -- a reference to a finding_id that doesn't exist is a fabrication, not a prediction, and is rejected rather than reported.

likelihood.description: Qualitative analyst judgement, deliberately not a fabricated-precision probability like EPSS -- this is prediction, not measurement.

confidence.description: The analyst's own confidence that this chain is a plausible attack path given the evidence, distinct from `likelihood` (how likely an attacker is to pursue it).

mitre_attack_techniques.description: ATT&CK technique/sub-technique IDs, only when the analyst can genuinely map a step to one -- an empty array is honest when none apply cleanly, not a gap to fill with a guess.

status.description: Fixed to the single allowed value. There is intentionally no schema-legal way to express 'confirmed', 'validated', or 'exploited' here -- this fleet does not attempt, test, or validate a predicted scenario, ever.

evidence_ref.description: Pointers into the chained findings' own evidence -- never new evidence from an attempt, since none is ever made.
